resources.string: RideMate is for adults only. India\'s data protection law and the licence of the AI model RideMate uses require this check.
You need to be 18 or older to use RideMate. Nothing was saved or sent from your phone.
Please read how RideMate uses your data. You can read this again any time in Settings → Privacy notice.
AI processing happens on Modal\'s servers in the USA.
Masked screenshots, notification text RideMate doesn\'t recognise, your destination text and voice transcripts may be processed outside India.
RideMate is made by Baharul Islam, an individual developer in Barpeta, Assam, India. Privacy contact and grievance officer: %1$s. We reply within 30 days.
You must be 18 or older to use RideMate. If we learn that someone under 18 is using it, we delete their data.

RideMate compares Uber, Ola and Rapido prices when you tap its button, watches those three apps\' notifications to remind you to cancel extra bookings, and guides you while you cancel them. It never taps or acts inside those apps. To read prices it uses Meta\'s Muse Spark Open AI model on Modal\'s cloud servers.
What RideMate uses, and for how long

• Pickup and drop places: kept on your phone and deleted a day after the ride. Your destination text is sent to Modal so the AI can pick the right place.
• If you include ONDC rides: their pickup and drop points are kept on our server only while needed, cleared within 1 hour if you don't book, otherwise when the ride ends or is cancelled.
• Screenshots of fare and ride screens: masked first, read by the AI on Modal, never stored.
• Addresses visible in those screenshots: masked where detected, otherwise sent with the masked image and processed only while it is read, never stored by RideMate.
• Text recognised on screen: on your phone only, for the ride session.
• Uber, Ola and Rapido notification text (masked): on your phone. Only notifications RideMate doesn't recognise, during a ride, are sent to Modal.
• Map tiles, only if you open the map: map tiles from OpenFreeMap see your IP and the area viewed.
• Your voice, only if you tap the mic: only the text transcript is sent to Modal, never the audio.
• Google email, name and photo, only if you sign in: kept by Firebase until you erase.
• A usage counter linked to a one-way code of your account: for fair use; kept 48 hours after you erase.
• IP address: for rate limits; 1 day.
• Ride outcome and request records (metadata only, no text, places or prices): 1 year.
• Crash reports, never with screen or notification text.
No ads, no advertising IDs, no marketing analytics, no contacts.

Before anything leaves your phone, RideMate blurs phone numbers, OTPs and PINs, number plates, names and your status bar. If a screen doesn\'t look like a fare or ride screen, nothing is uploaded. RideMate looks at your screen only when you tap its button, and Android asks your permission for each comparison.

AI processing happens on Modal\'s servers in the USA. RideMate\'s small server also runs on Modal. Sign-in, crash reports and remote settings are Google Firebase services; Firestore records are stored in Mumbai (asia-south1). Notification access is limited to Uber, Ola and Rapido; notifications from every other app are ignored.

Each permission is asked separately, with its reason. Google sign-in is optional: without it, you type prices yourself. You can withdraw consent any time: turn off a permission, sign out, use Settings → Erase, or email %1$s.

See what RideMate holds in Settings → My data. Ask us to correct or erase your data, nominate someone to act for you, or complain to us at %1$s (we reply within 30 days). If you\'re not satisfied, you can complain to the Data Protection Board of India.
Erase deletes your account, your RideMate data on this phone and on our server, except metadata logs (1 year, required by law) and an anonymous usage counter (48 h, abuse prevention).
Baharul Islam, Barpeta, Assam, India · %1$s (reply within 30 days)

RideMate reminds you to cancel extra bookings, so it needs to show notifications.
RideMate reads only Uber, Ola and Rapido notifications, to know when a driver accepts or cancels; every other app is ignored.
In the next screen, find \"RideMate ride guardian\" and turn it on, then come back.
Android blocks this switch for apps installed from outside the Play Store. RideMate will show you how to allow it in a moment.
RideMate\'s small floating button sits over the ride app, so you can tap it to read prices.
In the next screen, turn on \"Allow display over other apps\" for RideMate, then come back.
Android blocks some switches for apps installed from outside the Play Store until you allow them once.

1. Tap \"Open App info\".\n2. Tap ⋮ (top right), then \"Allow restricted settings\", and confirm with your PIN or fingerprint.\n3. Come back here and turn on notification access and the floating button.
RideMate fills in your pickup from where you are, only while you use the app.
Not now, I\'ll type my pickup
Battery saving can pause RideMate in the background, so cancel reminders might come late; allowing background running keeps them on time.
One more setting on your phone
Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones also stop apps on their own. Open Security → Autostart (or App info → Autostart) and turn on RideMate. Then in App info → Battery saver, choose \"No restrictions\".
Oppo, Realme and OnePlus phones also stop apps on their own. Open App info → Battery usage and turn on \"Allow background activity\" and \"Allow auto launch\".
Vivo and iQOO phones also stop apps on their own. Open i Manager → App manager → Autostart and turn on RideMate. Then in Battery → Background power consumption, allow RideMate.
Samsung phones may put unused apps to sleep. Open Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps, and add RideMate.
Motorola phones may limit background apps. Open App info → Battery and choose \"Unrestricted\" (or turn on \"Allow background usage\").
RideMate posts a test notification and checks that it can see it, so it won\'t miss a driver accepting.
